main_body: Thatched hut: a large hipped thatch roof (rows ~4-52) over a log-plank front wall with a central door (rows ~52-78).
top_band: Ochre/golden thatch slope from row ~4 to ~52, with a lighter bottom eave band and tapered side slopes. A dark eave line sits at rows ~52-54, then the log wall begins.
evidence: Reading a column through the middle: the thatch roof is a broad sloped top surface made of many shaded horizontal courses, and its flared hip sides show the slope. A lighter eave course ends it at about row 51, followed by a dark shadow row and the vertical log wall. The wall has a stone sill at the bottom. The door is inset, with a lintel, jambs and a dark interior, and a skull ornament sits on the roof. This matches how the reference houses show roof above wall, so it reads as a 3/4 building rather than a front elevation.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5 tones (highlight, light, mid, dark brown course lines, deep shadow at the right hip) plus per-course tick marks. The log wall has several browns with plank gradients, round shield medallions and a stone sill. Outlines lean dark brown and match the adjacent material, not black. The roof's courses repeat regularly and it has less per-tile variation than the tiled reference roofs, but it has no large flat fills and sits acceptably next to the reference.
